claims.statement: Every KV payload is a `codec.encode` JSON string (the host KV only accepts scalars), and all KV traffic is funnelled through `store.lua`, so changing the encoding changes exactly one module.

`role.index` is a dense ascending integer array rather than `{ id = true }`: a JSON object would return every integer key as a string, silently breaking membership tests, and KV has no delete or iteration face, so revoke only clears references and the index is append-only.

Bonuses are composed at read time (`effective` = base + role bonus + skill bonuses in ascending name order) and never written back into the entity attribute bag: writing back would make unequipping require undoing history, and `rank` deliberately does not scale the bonus.

The sliding window is a separate key family from the actor record: keeping it separate keeps the record's key set exactly `role`/`skills`/`counters`, avoids rewriting the whole ring on every `charge`, and cannot be derived from the monotonic `counters`.

Counters only increase and handlers return without writing when an id or record cannot be resolved, so a statistics event can never create a record out of thin air; event subscriptions install once, otherwise a double install doubles every counter.

`role.effective` costs exactly three `kv.get` calls at any actor count (record plus two definition tables), which is the structural evidence behind the O(1) claim rather than a wall-clock ratio alone.

The 28 counted cases (17 pre-S8 plus 11 S8 cases) are pinned by the fixture, and the compatibility assertion (`capacity-recharge-cap`) checks that the three-argument `recharge` returns byte-identical payloads.

The smoke file pins the export face (19 exports), the four event names and the four KV prefixes, and because the mock `ygg.emit` accepts tables, the real scalar-payload shape is checked separately by `cargo test -p ygg-sandbox --test packages_sandbox`.
